name: Absolics Inc.
old_description: When silicon hit a physical wall, we redefined the foundation of computing with glass
about:
Founded in 2018 in Covington, Georgia, Absolics Inc. is a semiconductor packaging company backed by South Korea's SK Group. The venture began under the leadership of CEO Jiho Kang with a mission to redefine computing foundations using glass substrates after silicon hit a physical scaling wall.

The company develops glass substrate platforms for next-generation semiconductor packaging, targeting AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. Its SVM facility in Covington serves as a test and manufacturing ground for high-density packaging. With a team of 16, Absolics operates globally from offices in London and Singapore, supported by $75 million in CHIPS Act manufacturing subsidies and $100 million in R&D funding.

Absolics serves the semiconductor industry, particularly companies advancing AI accelerators, high-performance computing processors, and advanced packaging solutions. Its customers include semiconductor manufacturers and packaging houses seeking alternatives to silicon substrates.

The company was started to overcome the physical scaling limits of silicon by using glass as a substrate material, offering better thermal dissipation and signal integrity for high-density packaging.
